Section 2.1: Rate of Change and Slope

Learning target: Students will interpret slope as a measure of constant rate of change.

WTC

What's to Come

U2-S21-WTC-001 · WTC · Section 2.1 · Family S21-WTC-SLOPE-STORY · WTC · Graph + Table + Context + Rate · constructed response

A cyclist rides at a steady pace. The graph and table describe the same trip.

Time (min)Distance (mi)
01
103
205
307
  1. Choose two points and compute change in distance divided by change in time.
  2. State the rate with units and explain what it means for the cyclist.
  3. Explain why using a different pair of points on this straight-line relationship gives the same rate.
  4. Decide whether a claim of 2 miles per minute is reasonable for this graph and explain.
Answer / solution

Using $(0,1)$ and $(10,3)$ gives $(3-1)/(10-0)=0.2$ mile per minute. The cyclist gains 0.2 mile each minute (2 miles every 10 minutes). Any two points on the same straight line have the same constant rate. A claim of 2 miles per minute is not reasonable; it is ten times the displayed rate.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: Students will interpret slope as a measure of constant rate of change.

Evidence/job: Preview slope as a constant rate across graph, table, units, and reasonableness.

Representation: Graph + Table + Context + Rate

Example 2

U2-S21-EX-002 · Notes Example · Section 2.1 · Family S21-POINT-SLOPE · EX · Ordered pairs + Ratio · constructed response

Find the slope through $(-2,5)$ and $(4,-7)$. Show a consistent subtraction order.

Answer / solution

$m=(-7-5)/(4-(-2))=-12/6=-2$.

Alignment / evidence

Evidence/job: Model a core slope/rate idea with visible reasoning.

Example 4

U2-S21-EX-004 · Notes Example · Section 2.1 · Family S21-CONTEXT-RATE · EX · Context + Rate · constructed response

A water tank drains 6 gallons every 4 minutes. Express the rate as a slope in gallons per minute and explain the sign.

Example 5

U2-S21-EX-005 · Notes Example · Section 2.1 · Family S21-SLOPE-ERROR · EX · Ordered pairs + Error analysis · constructed response

A student computes the slope from $(1,2)$ to $(5,10)$ as $(10-2)/(1-5)=-2$. Diagnose the error and calculate the correct slope.

Answer / solution

The student reversed the x-subtraction without also reversing the y-subtraction. Using the same point order gives $(10-2)/(5-1)=2$.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: I can apply slope calculations to interpret constant change between quantities.

Evidence/job: Model a core slope/rate idea with visible reasoning.

Representation: Ordered pairs + Error analysis

Example 6

U2-S21-EX-006 · Notes Example · Section 2.1 · Family S21-RATE-REASON · EX · Context + Rate · constructed response

A parking garage charge rises by 3 dollars per hour. A student says the slope should be 18 because the total after several hours is 18 dollars. Assess the claim.

Answer / solution

The slope is the change per hour, so 3 dollars per hour is the slope. A total such as 18 dollars is an output value, not the rate.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: I can determine whether a slope value is reasonable for a given context.

Evidence/job: Model a core slope/rate idea with visible reasoning.

Representation: Context + Rate

Section 2.2: Graphing Linear Functions

Learning target: Students will graph linear functions and interpret key features.

WTC

What's to Come

U2-S22-WTC-001 · WTC · Section 2.2 · Family S22-WTC-GRAPH-MODEL · WTC · Equation + Graph + Table + Context · constructed response

A music service charges a 6-dollar signup fee and 2 dollars per month. Let $C=2m+6$.

  1. Identify the starting value and monthly rate.
  2. Make a table for $m=0,1,2,3$.
  3. Use the table or slope-intercept information to sketch the graph.
  4. Explain what the point where the graph crosses the vertical axis means.
  5. Predict the cost after 8 months and decide whether that point belongs on a graph restricted to whole months.
Answer / solution

The starting value is 6 dollars and the rate is 2 dollars per month. The table outputs are 6, 8, 10, 12. The graph starts at $(0,6)$ and rises 2 for every 1 month. The vertical-axis intercept means the cost before any monthly charge. At 8 months, $C=22$ dollars; $(8,22)$ is a meaningful whole-month point.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: Students will graph linear functions and interpret key features.

Evidence/job: Preview graph construction and interpretation from slope/intercept information.

Representation: Equation + Graph + Table + Context

Stage / MG: Intro

Structure: WTC-FRQ-PREVIEW-01 · DOK 2-3 · Bloom Analyze

Section 2.3: Writing Linear Equations

Learning target: Students will write linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations.

WTC

What's to Come

U2-S23-WTC-001 · WTC · Section 2.3 · Family S23-WTC-WRITE-LINE · WTC · Graph + Table + Equation + Context · constructed response

A community garden water tank has 14 gallons at time 0 and gains water steadily.

Time (min)Water (gal)
014
220
426
632
  1. Find the rate of change from the table.
  2. Identify the starting value.
  3. Write an equation for water $W$ after $t$ minutes.
  4. Explain how the graph and table confirm both parameters.
  5. Rewrite your equation as $W-14=3t$ and explain why the two forms describe the same relationship.
Answer / solution

The rate is 3 gallons per minute and the starting value is 14 gallons. The equation is $W=3t+14$. The table has equal output change 6 for each 2 minutes, and the graph crosses the vertical axis at 14. Subtracting 14 from both sides gives the equivalent form $W-14=3t$.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: Students will write linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations.

Evidence/job: Preview equation writing from rate, initial value, table, graph, and equivalent form.

Representation: Graph + Table + Equation + Context

Section 2.4: Comparing Linear Representations

Learning target: Students will analyze and compare linear relationships using multiple representations.

WTC

What's to Come

U2-S24-WTC-001 · WTC · Section 2.4 · Family S24-WTC-COMPARE · WTC · Equation + Table + Graph + Context · constructed response

Two bike-rental shops use different pricing models. Shop A charges $A=6h+12$. Shop B is shown in the table.

Hours hShop B cost (dollars)
020
125
230
335
  1. Find the starting cost and hourly rate for each shop.
  2. Explain which shop starts cheaper and which grows faster.
  3. Determine the cost of each for 4 hours.
  4. Use rate and starting value evidence to explain whether one shop will always be cheaper.
Answer / solution

Shop A starts at 12 dollars and grows 6 dollars per hour. Shop B starts at 20 dollars and grows 5 dollars per hour. A starts cheaper but grows faster. At 4 hours, A costs 36 dollars and B costs 40 dollars. Because A has the larger slope, it eventually catches and passes B; solving $6h+12=5h+20$ gives $h=8$.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: Students will analyze and compare linear relationships using multiple representations.

Evidence/job: Preview comparison across unlike representations using rate and starting value.

Representation: Equation + Table + Graph + Context

U2-S24-P2-001 · Practice Set 2 · Section 2.4 · Family S24-EQ-COMPARE · F2-A1 · Equations · constructed response

Compare A: $y=2x+5$ and B: $y=2x+1$. Compare their rates of change and starting values; identify the larger of each.

Answer / solution

Rates: A=2, B=2; starts: A=5, B=1. Greater values follow from those comparisons.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: I can use slope and intercept information to interpret similarities and differences.

Evidence/job: Compare slope and intercept from equations.

Representation: Equations

Question 13

U2-S24-P2-013 · Practice Set 2 · Section 2.4 · Family S24-CONTEXT-COMPARE · F2-D1 · Context + Equations · constructed response

For a subscription, Relationship A starts at 10 and changes by 4 per month; Relationship B starts at 2 and changes by 7 per month. Compare the two relationships and determine which has the larger output after 3 months.

Answer / solution

A: start 10, rate 4; B: start 2, rate 7. At 3 months, A=22, B=23; B has the larger output.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: I can construct comparison models for linear relationships shown in different forms.

Evidence/job: Compare contextual linear models using common features.

Representation: Context + Equations

Question 14

U2-S24-P3-014 · Practice Set 3 · Section 2.4 · Family S24-CONTEXT-COMPARE · F3-D2 · Context + Equations · constructed response

For a rental, Relationship A starts at 5 and changes by 6 per hour; Relationship B starts at 20 and changes by 2 per hour. Compare the two relationships and determine which has the larger output after 3 hours.

Answer / solution

A: start 5, rate 6; B: start 20, rate 2. At 3 hours, A=23, B=26; B has the larger output.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: I can construct comparison models for linear relationships shown in different forms.

Evidence/job: Compare contextual linear models using common features.

Representation: Context + Equations

Question 1

U2-S24-EP-001 · Extra Practice · Section 2.4 · Family S24-EQ-COMPARE · F4-A1 · Equations · constructed response

Compare A: $y=2x+1$ and B: $y=2x-5$. Compare their rates of change and starting values; identify the larger of each.

Answer / solution

Rates: A=2, B=2; starts: A=1, B=-5. Greater values follow from those comparisons.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: I can use slope and intercept information to interpret similarities and differences.

Evidence/job: Compare slope and intercept from equations.

Representation: Equations

Section 2.5: Linear Modeling with Data

Learning target: Students will use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data.

WTC

What's to Come

U2-S25-WTC-001 · WTC · Section 2.5 · Family S25-WTC-DATA-MODEL · WTC · Scatter plot + Table + Equation + Context · constructed response

A class records outside temperature and the number of cold drinks sold during six lunch periods.

Temperature (°F)Drinks sold
5518
6021
6525
7028
7531
8035
  1. Describe the direction and approximate strength of the trend.
  2. Use the endpoints to estimate a reasonable slope in drinks per degree.
  3. Write a simple linear model using your slope and one data point.
  4. Use the model to predict sales near 72°F.
  5. Explain why predicting at 150°F would be less defensible.
Answer / solution

The trend is strong and positive. Using $(55,18)$ and $(80,35)$ gives an estimated slope $17/25\approx0.68$ drink per degree. A reasonable model is about $D=0.68T-19.4$ (other nearby lines are acceptable). At 72°F the prediction is about 30 drinks. A 150°F prediction is far outside the observed range, so the linear model has little support there.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: Students will use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data.

Evidence/job: Preview fitting, predicting, and judging a linear model from real data.

Representation: Scatter plot + Table + Equation + Context

U2-SUM-V1-Q10 · Secure Summative V1 · Section Summative · Family SUM-INTEGRATED · V1-INTEGRATED · Context + Equations + Comparison · constructed response

Plan A starts at 18 dollars and increases 3 dollars per use. Plan B starts at 6 dollars and increases 5 dollars per use. Write equations, determine when the plans cost the same, and explain which is cheaper before and after that point.

Answer / solution

$A=3x+18$, $B=5x+6$. They are equal when $3x+18=5x+6$, so $x=6$. Before 6 uses B is cheaper; after 6 uses A is cheaper.

Two printed graphs use different axis scales. A student chooses the visually steeper line as the larger rate. Explain a valid method for deciding instead.

Answer / solution

Read numerical coordinates from each graph and compute change in y divided by change in x using the labeled scales.

V5 Question 4

U2-SUM-V5-Q04 · Secure Summative V5 · Section Summative · Family SUM-ALT-COORD-CONTEXT · V5-ALT-COORD-CONTEXT · Context + Ordered pairs + Student-built graph · constructed response

A graph uses time (hours) on the horizontal axis and water (liters) on the vertical axis. It passes through $(0,30)$ and $(5,10)$. Find the slope with units, identify the intercept meaning, and sketch the graph.

Answer / solution

Slope $(10-30)/(5-0)=-4$ liters/hour. The intercept means 30 liters at time 0. The graph is a decreasing line through the two points.

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: Interpret and create coordinate-plane graphs, including ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts, in mathematical and contextual situations.

Evidence/job: Secure alternate-form evidence for the mapped Unit Mastery Goal.

Representation: Context + Ordered pairs + Student-built graph

V5 Question 6

U2-SUM-V5-Q06 · Secure Summative V5 · Section Summative · Family SUM-ALT-SPECIAL-SLOPE · V5-ALT-SPECIAL-SLOPE · Equations + Graph features · constructed response

Compare a horizontal line $y=5$ with a vertical line $x=5$. State the slope of each and explain why only one can be written as $y=mx+b$.

Answer / solution

$y=5$ has slope 0 and is $y=0x+5$. $x=5$ has undefined slope and cannot be written as a function of x in slope-intercept form.

Alignment / evidence

V5 Question 7

U2-SUM-V5-Q07 · Secure Summative V5 · Section Summative · Family SUM-ALT-CONTEXT-CROSS · V5-ALT-CONTEXT-CROSS · Context + Equations + Decision · constructed response

Company A charges 30 dollars plus 2 dollars per delivery. Company B charges 10 dollars plus 5 dollars per delivery. Determine the break-even number of deliveries and recommend a company for 4 deliveries and for 10 deliveries.

Answer / solution

$30+2d=10+5d$ gives $d=20/3\approx6.67$. At 4 deliveries B is cheaper (22 vs 38); at 10 A is cheaper (50 vs 60).

Alignment / evidence

Exact target: Compare relationships across equations, graphs, tables, visual patterns, and contexts and justify conclusions with representation evidence.

Evidence/job: Secure alternate-form evidence for the mapped Unit Mastery Goal.

U2-SUM-V5-Q09 · Secure Summative V5 · Section Summative · Family SUM-ALT-INTEGRATED-MODEL · V5-ALT-INTEGRATED-MODEL · Ordered pairs + Equation + Comparison · constructed response

A fundraiser records $(0,20),(2,30),(4,40)$ dollars for Team A. Team B follows $B=4t+28$. Write Team A’s model, compare rates and starting values, and decide which team has more at t=6.

Answer / solution

Team A: $A=5t+20$. A grows faster (5 vs 4), B starts higher (28 vs 20). At t=6, A=50 and B=52, so B still has more.

Alignment / evidence
